clue.text: More than one lot of characters needing to be sorted out

definitions.text: More than one lot of characters needing to be sorted out

parts.words: More than one lot of characters needing to be sorted out
parts.note: read cryptically, several groups of letters each waiting to be rearranged into a word are the puzzles a solver unscrambles

explanation.surface: Several batches of awkward people all need dealing with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people who need sorting out, but it means letters, and sorting them out is rearranging them.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural word puzzles made by rearranging letters: each is a lot of characters to be put in a new order.

clue.text: Close currently housing a bishop

indicators.note: housing means the word for currently holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: currently means now, at present
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation used for a bishop

explanation.surface: A cathedral close where a bishop is living at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a cathedral close but is the adjective, as in a close shave. RR (Right Reverend) for a bishop is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A close escape is a narrow one: both describe a margin that is tight or small.

clue.text: Clutch has g-grating noise

parts.note: the stuttered letter g at the start of g-grating gives the letter itself
a rasp is a harsh grating sound

explanation.surface: A clutch on a car makes a stuttering grinding noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'g-grating' supplies an extra G before the grating noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch something is to grip it tightly, synonym of seize.

clue.text: Humiliation in a place below stairs

parts.note: a basement is the storey at the foot of the stairs, below ground level

explanation.surface: A servant feels humbled working below stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below stairs' suggests the servants' quarters of a big house, which fits the humiliation of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliation is a lowering of someone's dignity, the sense of debasing oneself.

clue.text: Person in kingdom could be starting a sentence

explanation.surface: Someone in a realm may be about to begin a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests prison, but it is grammar: a sentence often begins with its grammatical subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's people are his or her subjects; in grammar the subject is the noun a sentence usually opens with.

clue.text: Is imprisoned by goddess, getting maltreatment

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the word is is locked inside the goddess word

parts.note: a Muse is one of nine Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: Someone jailed by a deity suffers cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Maltreatment is wrong or harmful handling, synonym of abuse.

clue.text: Maiden aims to effect repairs

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase; read as he or she effects repairs, matching the third-person verb

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
ends are aims or goals, as in ends and means

explanation.surface: A young woman sets out to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect repairs is to fix or patch up what is broken.

clue.text: Senior politicians finding means test silly

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of means test are knocked into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Elder statesmen consider the benefits means test absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: A means test is a check of income before benefits are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced, respected political leaders are the elder figures of government.

clue.text: It's not a hard job making home safe outside

indicators.note: outside means the safe word goes round the home word

parts.note: secure means safe
in means at home

explanation.surface: Keeping a house secure is an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: A post with pay but little or no work is the classic easy number.

clue.text: Time to admit despicable person's mistakes

indicators.note: to admit means the time word lets the despicable person in

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a despicable person; the 's is read as is, a link

explanation.surface: It is time for a scoundrel to own up to his errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing errors listed for correction, a Latin plural.

clue.text: Item of clothing shown by girl at back of group

indicators.note: at back of places the girl after the group word

parts.note: a band is a group, especially of musicians
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A singer at the rear of a pop group is seen in some garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A large patterned scarf worn round the head or neck is a piece of apparel.

clue.text: Fully equipped learner in attempt to win prize

indicators.note: in places the learner inside the word for trying to win

parts.note: to compete is to try to win a prize
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A well-kitted novice is trying to win an award.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with every part it needs is whole, synonym of entire.

clue.text: Observe child keeping quiet — this not allowed?

indicators.note: keeping means the observe-and-child pair holds the quiet letter

parts.note: to observe is to see
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Watch a child kept silent, since talking is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: what is not allowed when a child is kept quiet is talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking, the faculty of uttering words, is what is banned when silence is enforced.

clue.text: Raise doubts about person who wrote second gospel?

definitions.text: Raise doubts about person who wrote second gospel?

parts.note: to question something is to raise doubts about it
Mark is the evangelist credited with the second gospel

explanation.surface: Someone casts doubt on the authorship of Mark's gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself ends in the punctuation it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol ending a query, the very mark printed at the end of this clue.

clue.text: Style of furniture befitting a bountiful monarch

explanation.surface: Furniture fit for a generous king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Anne's Bounty was a fund the British monarch set up in 1704 for poor clergy, hence a bountiful monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An early 18th-century English style of furniture is named after the queen who reigned then and founded a church charity.

clue.text: NCOs sort out falsehoods

parts.note: to order is to sort out or arrange
lies are falsehoods

explanation.surface: Sergeants deal with untrue stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Military attendants, often corporals or sergeants detailed to serve officers, are non-commissioned soldiers.

clue.text: Very drowsy mate coos, going off

indicators.note: going off suggests the letters of mate coos go bad and fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A friend's cooing makes one drift into sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: In a deep unconscious state, or loosely, extremely sleepy.

clue.text: Meeting of witches granted new location in London

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

indicators.note: new means the letters of granted are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gathering of witches is given a new venue in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: COVENT GARDEN is a London district famous for its market and opera house; 'new' turns GRANTED into TGARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known area of central London, home to the Royal Opera House.

clue.text: Woman given power — little man adjusted

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
P is the physics symbol for power
Ted is a short form of a man's name such as Edward

explanation.surface: A woman given authority has a small man tweaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered to suit new conditions, synonym of modified.

clue.text: Courteous man from Warsaw, say, embracing Italian

indicators.note: embracing means the Warsaw man holds the Italian inside

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, of which Warsaw is the capital

explanation.surface: A gracious Polish man hugs an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous behaviour is well-mannered and respectful, synonym of civil.

clue.text: After open hostility Edmund is cautioned

indicators.note: after places Edmund's short name behind the hostility word

parts.note: war is open hostility
Ned is a pet form of Edmund

explanation.surface: Following a fight, Edmund receives a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cautioned is being given notice of danger or reprimand.

clue.text: Prepare university to be released from constraint

indicators.note: to be released from means the university letter gets out of the constraint word

parts.note: duress is constraint or compulsion

explanation.surface: Get a university out of its restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' as in dress a salad or dress a wound: getting it ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress food or a wound is to get it ready, a cooking or nursing sense.

clue.text: A garment's being worn to cover one graze

indicators.note: to cover means the a-garment-worn run goes round the one letter

parts.note: bra's: a bra is a garment, the 's kept as S
on means being worn
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone's underwear chafes, leaving a scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape on the skin from rubbing, synonym of graze.

clue.text: Remove muck from farmer's courtyard

indicators.note: from tells the solver to pull letters out of farmer's courtyard

explanation.surface: Clean the dirt out of a farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub hard to clean off dirt, synonym of scrub.

clue.text: Gloomy round of an Ulster cop?

parts.note: County Down is one of the six counties of Ulster in Northern Ireland
a beat is the round a police officer patrols

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish policeman's patrol is depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The cop's round is his beat, and 'Ulster' points to County Down in Northern Ireland, so the cop's beat there is a Down beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat means pessimistic or dispirited, synonym of glum.

clue.text: Club with very cold water but no English bitter?

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: but no means the English letter is dropped from the frozen water

parts.note: ice is very cold, frozen water

explanation.surface: A golfer with icy water but no English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like British beer; the question mark flags the sense of wryly sardonic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardonic remark is mocking and wry, which can shade into bitterness.

clue.text: Odds against son appearing in rugby competition

indicators.note: against places the son letter beside the odds

parts.note: evens are betting odds of one to one

explanation.surface: A bookmaker offers even money on a son playing in a rugby tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENS is rugby played seven a side, with tournaments such as the Hong Kong Sevens.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-a-side form of rugby, played in short tournaments.

clue.text: Group around king in action did a bunk

indicators.note: in places the group-and-king run inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: around means the group word wraps the king letter

parts.note: a set is a group
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A gang surrounding a monarch fled mid-battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did a bunk' is British slang for ran away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran off and abandoned one's post, slang for absconded.
